turns.text:
I’ll run the inverse design with the specified bounds, then check the candidates against the strength, yield stress, and clinker objective.
The first search found candidates at 70% OPC, but their median predicted yield stress is below the requested range. I’ll check whether a lower OPC fraction is feasible within the same material bounds before choosing a recommendation.
The lowest-OPC candidate found is **55% OPC, 15% silica fume, and 30% limestone powder** by binder mass, with **w/b 0.396** and **sand/binder 1.27**. It reaches the lowest OPC fraction allowed by those binder bounds.

| Target | Model prediction, q50 [q10, q90] | Estimated chance of meeting target |
|---|---:|---:|
| 28-day compressive strength ≥40 MPa | 45.0 [25.3, 71.6] MPa | 0.63 |
| Static yield stress 1–4 kPa | 0.459 [0.00965, 4.515] kPa | 0.30 |

**This is a screening candidate, not a confirmed printable mix.** Its median predicted yield stress is below 1 kPa, and the estimated chance of meeting both targets is 0.189. The yield-stress interval is very wide. Published 3D-printing mortar analogues met both measured targets, but their compositions fall outside parts of your search space; for example, [RFA-50](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2025.144187) reported 44.6 MPa at 28 days and 1.76 kPa static yield stress.

The search used 28 days, a 50-mm cube strength comparison, moist curing, 3DCP conditions, and yield stress at zero rest time. Sand/binder was selected by the design engine because you did not set it. A physical printability verdict needs a nozzle, layer geometry, target height, and printing schedule. Measure fresh yield stress and strength before adopting the mix.
